title: A Simple Protocol for Periodic Live Cell Observation of Flagellate Stages in the Lichen Alga Trebouxia
author: Enrico Boccato
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Trebouxia decolorans Ahmadjian [Culture Collection of the University of Trieste (Italy), originally isolated from Xanthoria parietina (L.) Th. Fr.]
T. gelatinosa Ahmadjian [Culture Collection of the University of Trieste (Italy), originally isolated from Flavoparmelia caperata (L.) Hale]
T. vagua Voytsekhovich & Beck [Culture Collection of the University of Trieste (Italy), originally isolated from Bagliettoa marmorea (Scop.) Gueidan & Cl. Roux]

Note: All Trebouxia strains were cultivated on solid Trebouxia medium (TM, see Recipes) in Microbox Junior 40 vessels and subcultured every 3 weeks. Vessels were kept in a thermostatic chamber at 16 ± 1 °C and 23 ± 1 μmol photons·m -2 ·s -1 with a 12/12 h light/dark regime [1]. Reagents
Trebouxia medium (TM) (see Recipes) Recipes The BBM is prepared starting from the stock solutions listed in the Reagent column of Recipe

For the trace elements, EDTA, and Fe solutions, detailed recipes are provided below (see Recipes 1–3). All the following stock solutions can be stored at 4 °C in glass bottles for at least 2–3 months after preparation. We recommend using autoclaved tips each time an aliquot is taken from the stock solutions and using different tips for each solution to avoid possible contamination and cross-contamination. If contamination is detected in a stock solution, discard it and prepare a fresh one before using it for the preparation of BBM or TM.

steps.title: Prepare trace elements stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve ZnSO₄·7H₂O (0.441 g), MnCl₂·4H₂O (0.072 g), MoO₃ (0.0355 g), CuSO₄·5H₂O (0.0785 g) and Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (0.0245 g) in de‑ionised water to a final volume of 50 mL (final concentrations: 8.82 g/L, 1.44 g/L, 0.71 g/L, 1.57 g/L, 0.49 g/L respectively). Autoclave if needed for dissolution.

steps.title: Prepare EDTA stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve EDTANa₂ (2.5 g) and KOH (1.55 g) in de‑ionised water to a final volume of 50 mL (final concentrations: 50 g/L and 31 g/L respectively).

steps.title: Prepare iron stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve FeSO₄·7H₂O (0.249 g) in de‑ionised water, then add H₂SO₄ (96 %) 0.05 mL (1 mL per L of stock) and bring to 50 mL (final FeSO₄ concentration 4.98 g/L). Add acid to water, never water to acid.

steps.title: Prepare Bold’s basal medium (BBM)
steps.instruction: For 1 L, add 10 mL each of 25 g/L NaNO₃, 7.5 g/L MgSO₄·7H₂O, 2.5 g/L NaCl, 7.5 g/L K₂HPO₄, 17.5 g/L KH₂PO₄, 2.5 g/L CaCl₂·2H₂O, 1 mL of 11.4 g/L H₃BO₃, 1 mL trace‑elements stock, 1 mL EDTA stock, 1 mL Fe stock, and de‑ionised water to 936 mL. Add agar (15 g/L) gradually while stirring; agar will dissolve only during autoclaving. Bring to 1 L, store at 4 °C, and autoclave (standard cycle) before use.

steps.title: Prepare Trebouxia medium (TM)
steps.instruction: Pour 500 mL liquid BBM into a 1 L glass bottle with a magnetic stir bar. While stirring, add NaNO₃ (0.5 g), casein‑yeast peptone (10 g), and D‑(+)-glucose (20 g) until fully dissolved. For solid TM, add agar (15 g/L) gradually, noting it will dissolve only during autoclaving. Bring the volume to 1 L with BBM. Prepare fresh before use; store solid TM at 4 °C and inspect for contamination.

steps.title: Autoclave BBM and accessories
steps.instruction: Place hot BBM, razor blades, a 200 mL beaker, a 600 mL beaker containing slides, 5 µL and 5 mL pipette tips, and pieces of 40 µm nylon net into individual aluminium‑foil wraps, then into Steripack® pouches. Seal and autoclave 21 min at 121 °C, 1.1 bar.

steps.title: UV‑sterilise external surfaces
steps.instruction: In a biological hood, expose 9‑cm Petri dishes, disposable syringes, and disposable loops to UV light for 20 min, then switch on the hood’s laminar flow for a further 20 min. Open sterile Petri dishes only inside the hood.

steps.title: Cool BBM to safe handling temperature
steps.instruction: After autoclaving, transfer all sterilised materials to the hood. Wait until BBM temperature is ≥90 °C but ≤60 °C before handling to avoid boiling liquids and premature solidification.

steps.title: Cast BBM layer on slides
steps.instruction: Place a glass microscopy slide in a Petri dish and pour ≈25 mL hot liquid BBM to cover the slide with a ~2 mm thick layer.

steps.title: Trim excess BBM
steps.instruction: When the BBM has solidified, trim the edges of the slide with a sterile razor blade and discard the excess medium.

steps.title: Optional slide storage
steps.instruction: Seal trimmed slides in Petri dishes with Parafilm® (inside the hood) and store at 4 °C for up to 3–4 weeks.

steps.title: Mark slide orientation
steps.instruction: Remove a small portion of the BBM layer from one side to expose glass, then mark the slide (e.g., with a waterproof marker) to keep a constant orientation for microscopy.

steps.title: Prepare moist absorbent paper
steps.instruction: Moisten 100 % cellulose absorbent paper with sterile de‑ionised water until evenly moist but not dripping.

steps.title: Line Petri dishes with paper
steps.instruction: Line the bottom of each Petri dish containing a slide with the moist absorbent paper to maintain high humidity (system remains sterile for up to 14 days).

steps.title: Sterilise TM vessels
steps.instruction: Place Microbox Junior 40 vessels in Steripack® pouches, seal, and autoclave together with the TM solution (same 21 min, 121 °C, 1.1 bar cycle).

steps.title: Transfer hot TM to hood
steps.instruction: After autoclaving, move all sterilised TM and vessels to the biological hood, observing the same temperature precautions as for BBM.

steps.title: Solidify TM in vessels
steps.instruction: Pour hot TM into the vessels and allow it to solidify at room temperature (≈30 min). Store vessels at 4 °C, inspecting each for contamination before use.

steps.title: Harvest algal cells
steps.instruction: After 3 weeks growth on solid TM, collect 0.4 g of cells from each vessel with a sterile disposable loop; determine fresh weight by transferring to a pre‑weighed Falcon® tube and weighing on an analytical balance.

steps.title: Prepare algal suspension in BBM
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL liquid BBM to a sterile 15 mL Falcon® tube, introduce the collected cells, then top up with additional BBM to a final volume of 15 mL. The cells will form clumps.

steps.title: Assemble syringe filter
steps.instruction: Attach a 40 µm nylon mesh to the tip of a needle‑less syringe and secure it with the plastic plug from a syringe needle.

steps.title: Homogenise algal suspension
steps.instruction: Remove the plunger, pour the algal suspension into the syringe, and gently push it through the nylon mesh with light pressure to break up aggregates. If clumps remain too large, pre‑filter through a 100 µm mesh.

steps.title: Inoculate BBM‑coated slides
steps.instruction: Using a 0.5–10 µL pipette with autoclaved tips, place 5 µL of the homogenised suspension onto the BBM layer of each slide as a small droplet. Up to 2–3 droplets may be placed per slide; do not cover with a coverslip.

steps.title: Incubate inoculated slides
steps.instruction: Return slides to Petri dishes lined with moist paper and incubate at 20 ± 1 °C, under 23 ± 1 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ light, with a 12/12 h light/dark cycle.

steps.title: Place slides on microscope
steps.instruction: Mount the inoculated BBM‑coated slides on the stage of a light microscope.

steps.title: Identify regions of interest
steps.instruction: Scan the slide surface, locate cell groups to be monitored, and record their coordinates using the microscope’s coordinate system.

steps.title: Acquire images or videos
steps.instruction: Capture images and/or videos of the selected cells with the microscope‑attached camera. Note that sterility may be lost after the first observation if the microscope is not in a sterile environment.

steps.title: Return slides to incubation
steps.instruction: Place the slides back into their Petri dishes with moist paper and continue incubation under the same conditions.

steps.title: Repeat daily observations
steps.instruction: Perform daily microscopy of the same cell groups, noting that algal growth will increase crowding; daily monitoring ensures reliable identification over time.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol was used and validated in the following research article: • Boccato et al. [1]. Zoospore diversity and sexual reproduction in the lichen-forming genus Trebouxia : From neglected motile cells to new evidence of sexual stages. Plant Biology (Figures 1–4, Figures S1–S2, Table S1, and Videos S1–S8). The use of this system made it possible to successfully observe the development and behaviour of live flagellate cells over several days. The reproducibility of the method was demonstrated for four Trebouxia species ( T. decolorans, T. gelatinosa, T. vagua , and T. angustilobata ), belonging to three phylogenetic clades.
